collection.description: A midwife wonders whether distant scholars might understand why children sometimes resemble parents and sometimes differ greatly.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A midwife wonders whether distant scholars might understand why children sometimes resemble parents and sometimes differ greatly.

a1.name: Outcome A1
a1.text: Researchers propose that living things carry tiny patterns passed between generations.

a2.name: Outcome A2
a2.text: A villager cautions that family resemblance cannot explain everything about a person.

b1.name: Outcome B1
b1.text: The midwife hopes such knowledge could help explain certain inherited conditions without blaming families.

b2.name: Outcome B2
b2.text: An elder worries that people might misuse it to rank or exclude others; the scholars agree that knowledge brings responsibility.

c1.name: Outcome C1
c1.text: A parent says affection, experience, and choice also shape a life.

text_only.reason: "experience" in its everyday sense (what a person has lived through), not a skill gain

c2.name: Outcome C2
c2.text: A child asks whether knowing every inherited trait would reveal someone's future; the adults admit it would not.
